learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: perpendicular force
items.prompt: A 40 N upward force acts while an object moves 3 m horizontally. How much work does that force do?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: parallel pull
items.prompt: A constant 15 N force pulls in the direction of a 4 m displacement. What work does it do?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: oblique force
items.prompt: A 30 N force acts 60° from a 6 m displacement. Use cos60° = 0.50. What is the work?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: opposing force
items.prompt: A 9 N force points exactly opposite a 7 m displacement. What work does it do?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: angled tow
items.prompt: A 50 N tow force acts 60° above a 10 m horizontal displacement. Use cos60° = 0.50. What work does the tow force do?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: infer angle
items.prompt: A 20 N force acts over 5 m and does +50 J of work. Which included angle is consistent?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: select included angle
items.prompt: A force points left while displacement points right. What angle belongs in W = Fd cosθ?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: angled push
items.prompt: A 24 N force acts 60° from an 8 m displacement. Use cos60° = 0.50. What work is done?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: recover cosine
items.prompt: Which expression isolates cosθ from W = Fd cosθ?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: infer opposing angle
items.prompt: A 10 N force acts over 4 m and does −40 J of work. Which angle is consistent?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: net work
items.prompt: An applied force does +45 J and friction does −20 J. What is the net work?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: update kinetic energy
items.prompt: An object begins with 30 J of kinetic energy and experiences −12 J of net work. What is its final kinetic energy?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: infer speed trend
items.prompt: What does +80 J of net work imply for an object's kinetic energy?
options: It stays fixed because work is scalar
It becomes exactly 80 J regardless of its initial value
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: conservative distinction
items.prompt: Which property identifies work by a conservative force between two fixed endpoints?
options: It always has a positive sign
It is independent of the path taken
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: final speed
items.prompt: A 2.0 kg object starts at 2.0 m/s. An applied force does +18 J and friction does −6 J. What final speed results?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: compare paths
items.prompt: Two paths connect the same starting and ending heights, but path B is longer. Gravity and kinetic friction act. Which statement is correct?
options: Gravity does different work because path B is longer; friction does equal work
Both gravity and friction do endpoint-only work
Gravity: equal work; friction: more negative on path B
Neither force does work because endpoints match
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: theorem setup
items.prompt: Which equation correctly combines multiple force contributions?
options: Ki = Kf + ΣWforces for every sign
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: new final speed
items.prompt: A 1.0 kg object starts at 4.0 m/s. Net work of +10 J acts. What is its final speed?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: path dependence
items.prompt: Which work contribution changes when travel distance changes but gravitational endpoints remain fixed?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: two ramps
items.prompt: Two ramps reach the same vertical height. Ramp 2 is twice as long and both have the same kinetic-friction magnitude. Compared with ramp 1, what work is done on ramp 2?
options: Same gravity work; twice the negative friction work
Twice the gravitational work and same friction work
Half the gravitational work and no friction work
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: kinetic energy
items.prompt: What is the kinetic energy of a 2.0 kg object moving at 3.0 m/s?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: gravitational energy
items.prompt: Use g = 10 m/s². How much does gravitational potential energy increase when a 3 kg mass rises 4 m?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: spring energy
items.prompt: A spring with k = 200 N/m is compressed 0.10 m. How much energy is stored?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: arbitrary reference
items.prompt: What changes if the zero-height reference for gravitational potential energy is moved upward by 2 m?
options: All physical speed predictions must change
Ug labels shift; predictions do not
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: falling object
items.prompt: Use g = 10 m/s². An object starts from rest and falls 20 m with no losses. What speed does it reach?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: spring, rise, and loss
items.prompt: A spring initially stores 50 J. It launches a 1 kg object upward so the object gains 20 J of gravitational potential energy while friction removes 5 J. What final kinetic energy remains?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: write state balance
items.prompt: For a lossless fall from rest with final height chosen as zero, which equation is correct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: new drop
items.prompt: Use g = 10 m/s². An object starts from rest and falls 5 m without losses. What speed results?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: place nonconservative work
items.prompt: Which balance includes signed nonconservative work?
options: Ki − Ui = Kf − Uf regardless of friction
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: spring and friction
items.prompt: A spring releases 36 J. An object gains 8 J of gravitational potential and friction removes 4 J. What final kinetic energy results?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: average power
items.prompt: A device transfers 600 J in 3.0 s. What is its average power?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: equal work, different time
items.prompt: Two devices each do 1000 J of work. Device A takes 5 s and B takes 10 s. Which has greater average power?
options: B, by a factor of two
A, by a factor of two
They have equal power because work is equal
Power cannot be compared without force
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: ideal input distance
items.prompt: An ideal machine lifts a 400 N load by 0.50 m using a 100 N input force. How far must the input move?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: calculate efficiency
items.prompt: A machine receives 800 J and delivers 600 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: lift and power
items.prompt: An ideal machine raises a 500 N load 2.0 m in 4.0 s using a 250 N input force. What input distance and average output power are required?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: compare devices
items.prompt: Devices A and B each deliver 400 J. A takes 4 s with 80% efficiency; B takes 8 s with 50% efficiency. Which statement is correct?
options: A: 100 W, 500 J input; B: 50 W, 800 J input
A and B have equal power because output work matches
A requires 320 J input and B requires 200 J input
B is more efficient because it runs longer
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: separate ratios
items.prompt: Which pairing is correct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: new ideal lift
items.prompt: An ideal machine lifts 300 N through 1.5 m in 3.0 s using 150 N input. What input distance and output power result?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: input from efficiency
items.prompt: Which equation finds input work from useful output work and efficiency η?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: compare pumps
items.prompt: Pump C delivers 300 J in 3 s at 60% efficiency. Pump D delivers 300 J in 6 s at 75% efficiency. Which is correct?
options: C: 100 W and 500 J input; D: 50 W and 400 J input
C and D: 50 W and 300 J input each
C: 60 W and 180 J input; D: 75 W and 225 J input
D has greater output power and requires more input energy
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
